701227.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂énti (“front, opposite”). Cognates include English and, Latin ante, Sanskrit अन्ति (ánti), and Old Armenian ընդ (ənd).

701215.t: From ἀντί (antĭ́, “in return for”) + ἀποδίδωμι (ăpodĭ́dōmi, “to give back”).

701236.t: Koine adjective, from an ancient neuter ἀντίθετον (antítheton, “rhetorical antithesis”) . Deverbal from ἀντιτίθημι (ăntĭtĭ́thēmĭ, “set against”) (ἀντι- (anti-) + stem θε- as in τίθημι (títhēmi) - θετός (thetós)) + -τος (-tos).

701251.t: From ἀντίος (antíos): the adverb/preposition is from the adverbial accusative, and the noun is from the neuter singular.

701242.t: Assuming a compound with ἀντι- (anti-, “opposite, against”) does not help much; the connection with ἀντικρούω (antikroúō, “to come into collision”), suggested by Kretschmer, is improbable, as are other attempts, like a derivation from ἀντι- (anti-,…

701294.t: From Proto-Indo-European *senh₂- (“to seek, accomplish, work on, succeed”). Cognate with Sanskrit सन् (san, “to gain, acquire, be successful”), as well as perhaps Hittite 𒊭𒀭𒄴𒍣 (ša-an-aḫ-zi, “to seek”).

701205.t: From ἀντι- (anti-, “against”) + ἀγωνίζομαι (agōnízomai, “contend for a prize”).
